author: FREE PRESS STAFF
title: Boy bitten by shark recovering well - NewsBreak
text:
By FREE PRESS STAFF ,
8 hours ago KEY LARGO — An 8-year-old boy bitten by a shark snorkeling off Key Largo last week is recovering well following surgery to his leg, according to his family.
Richard Burrows was snorkeling with his father, David, and older sister, Rose, 10, around 3:30 p.m. on Monday, Sept. 1, when a black tip shark rushed the trio and bit the boy on his right knee.
The initial injury inflicted on the boy was significant, but due to the help of a number of people, it was contained, according to a statement issued Wednesday, Sept. 3, by the family.
"Richard is recovering well from his surgery and is gaining strength by the day. He is in good spirits," the family noted. "Our hope is that he will be back enjoying his passion for the ocean and marine life with his older sister in no time."
The statement credited the boy's sister for her quick response to his injury.
"Rose was instrumental in her brother’s rescue and both of her parents are immensely proud of the strength of character and composure she demonstrated under pressure," the statement noted.
Trauma Star airlifted the injured boy to Jackson Memorial Hospital in Miami, according to the Monroe County Sheriff's Office.
The U.S. Coast Guard and the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission were notified of the incident.
Following the incident, the Burrows family extended its thanks to all those involved in the youngster's rescue, particularly Monroe County Sheriff Rick Ramsey and his department, Monroe County Fire Rescue, Richard Hayden from Horizon Divers, Garden Cove Marina, the Trauma Star Air Ambulance flight crew and paramedics, and the teams at Jackson Memorial Hospital Ryder Trauma Center, led by Dr. Vincente Nelson, surgical critical care, and Dr. Brian Grottkau, chief of pediatric orthopedics.
"The Burrows family sincerely appreciate and thank everyone for their messages of support and well wishes and assistance in these past days," the statement concluded. "We now request some privacy for the family to focus solely on Richard's recovery and will not be commenting further.”
